title: Where are you from?
goal: Say which country and city you're from, ask where others are from, and recognize the gender of a Bulgarian noun just from its last letter — knowledge you'll use in every unit after this one.
bekal: say nationalities in their male and female forms
guess a noun's gender from its last letter
respond to a welcome the right way

dialogs.title: Диалог — At a café near campus
dialogs.intro: Ani is sitting in a café in Sofia and works up the courage to talk to the woman at the next table. Notice that the word for "Bulgarian person" changes shape depending on who you're talking about.

lines.speaker: Мария:
lines.id: Yes, I'm Bulgarian. From Plovdiv. And where are you from?
lines.literal: yes, Bulgarian-woman — am. from — Plovdiv. and — you — from-where — are?

lines.speaker: Мария:
lines.id: Indonesia! That's very far. What's it like there?
lines.literal: Indonesia! much — far. how — is — there?

lines.speaker: Мария:
lines.id: And here it's cold, isn't it?

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: A little. But Sofia is a lovely city.
lines.literal: a-little. but — Sofia — is — lovely — city.

lines.speaker: Мария:
lines.id: Thank you! I'm Maria. I'm a teacher.
lines.literal: thank-you! I — am — Maria. teacher-(f) — am.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: I'm Ani, a student. Nice to meet you.
lines.literal: I — am — Ani, student-(f). pleasant — to-me — is.

lines.speaker: Мария:
lines.literal: also — to — me. well — come-(f) — in — Bulgaria!

notes: **Nationality follows the gender of the PERSON, not the country.** A man is a *българин*, a woman is a *българка*. ⚠️ This is a classic slip: English has one word for everyone — "Bulgarian" — so learners end up using *българин* for a woman. It sounds as jarring as calling a woman "sir".

**Almost all country names end in -ия and are feminine.** *Индонезия, България, Русия, Италия, Германия.* Those that don't end in -ия are usually still feminine if they end in -а: *Америка, Гърция*. Exceptions worth remembering: *Китай* (China) and *Виетнам* are masculine, while *Мароко* is neuter.

**Много means both "much/many" AND "very".** *Много хора* = many people; *много далече* = very far. Bulgarian doesn't distinguish the two, so you'll use this one word constantly. Its opposite is *малко* — "a little", also "a bit, rather".

**Нали is Bulgarian's "isn't it?", and it never changes.** English demands *isn't it? / don't you? / haven't we?*, switching every time; Bulgarian has a single word for all of them, like a tag "right?". One big burden simply gone.

**Добре дошъл / дошла / дошли — even "welcome" follows gender.** To a man: *Добре дошъл!* To a woman: *Добре дошла!* To more than one person: *Добре дошли!* ⚠️ The reply isn't "thank you" but **Добре заварил** (said by a man) or **Добре заварила** (by a woman) — literally "well I've found (you, in good health)". Answering *благодаря* isn't wrong, but answering *добре заварила* will make people pleasantly surprised.

**Тук and там — "here" and "there", with no change of form.** Russian uses different words for "here" and "to here"; Bulgarian doesn't. *Тук* covers both — just like English "come here" / "I'm here". It's the first of many simplifications that make Bulgarian lighter than its relatives.

**Weather sentences have no subject.** *Топло е* — "warm is", with no word for "it" or "the weather". English needs a dummy "it" ("it's warm"); Bulgarian doesn't. The only thing that must stay is *е*.

grammars.title: Three noun genders — recognize them by the last letter
body: Every Bulgarian noun has a gender, and you can almost always guess it from the last letter. This isn't decorative knowledge: the definite article, adjectives and numbers all adjust to it. Invest five minutes in this table and the next ten units get much lighter.
after: The most common exceptions: a small group of feminine nouns ending in a consonant — *вечер* (evening), *нощ* (night), *пролет* (spring), *есен* (autumn), *сол* (salt), *любов* (love). There aren't many; learn these six and the rest will rarely trouble you.

⚠️ English has no noun gender at all, so this instinct has to be built from scratch. The good news: **learn each word together with its last letter**, not with a "masculine/feminine" label. If you know a word ends in -а, you automatically know the rest.

grammars.title: Откъде сте? — where you're from
body: One preposition, **от**, is all you need, and the place name never changes form. Compare Russian, where every preposition demands a different form of the noun.
after: Look at the last two rows: **в** means "in" **and** "to", and the city name doesn't change one bit. The verb tells you which is meant — *живея* (I live) means staying put, *отивам* (I go) means moving. Where English needs two prepositions, Bulgarian lets the verb do the work.

blocks.text: Three columns, three different forms from the same root. Notice that language names always end in **-ски** and are never capitalized.

⚠️ The word for German, **немски**, looks nothing like the country name *Германия*. Its root is the old Slavic word *ням* — "mute": people whose language we can't understand. The same oddity runs through all the Slavic languages.

To say "I speak language X", the language word takes the prefix **по-**: *Говоря по български* (I speak Bulgarian), *Говорите ли по английски?* (Do you speak English?). Without *по-*, *български език* means "the Bulgarian language" as a thing.

blocks.text: If someone asks *Харесва ли ти София?* (Do you like Sofia?) and you can't give a long answer yet, two words are enough: **Много хубаво!** People will smile and keep talking — and that's how real learning happens.

exercises.prompt: Write the gender of each noun: м (masculine), ж (feminine), or ср (neuter).
Put the words in the right order.

items: Мария е от София. Тя е ____.
Иван е от София. Той е ____.
Ани е от Джакарта. Тя е ____.
Джон е от Лондон. Той е ____.
Юки е от Токио. Тя е ____.

answers: Откъде сте? — От Индонезия съм. — Тя е българка. — София е хубав град. — Тук е студено, нали? — Добре дошла в България!
От Индонезия съм. — Много далече е. — София е хубав град. — Вие българка ли сте? — Живея в София.
